page: Amazon Web Services c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 vCPUs, consisting of 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and includes dedicated CPU allocation. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2989.57. However, multi-core CPU performance is weaker, falling into the bottom 25% with a score of 5977.67. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the Passmark memory score is poor, falling in the bottom 10%, and memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks register in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance, while multi-threaded decompression and software compilation are weak.

The c6a.xlarge offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or high memory bandwidth. While its single-core processing is strong, the low memory-to-CPU ratio and weak multi-core scaling limit its utility for memory-intensive databases or heavy parallel processing. This instance is best suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight web serving, basic text processing, or small-scale LLM inference text generation where a 135M model can achieve an average of 137.92 tokens per second.
